metadata.title: Artifact for "Breaking the Generative Steganography Trilemma: ANStega for Optimal Capacity, Efficiency, and Security"
metadata.description:
Hardware and other requirements

This artifact's performance evaluation requires an NVIDIA GPU. The core of the research involves running inference on Large Language Models (LLMs), which is not feasible for evaluation on commodity CPUs.

  • Paper Replication Hardware (High-End): To replicate the exact performance metrics (e.g., ES, GS) for the largest models reported in the paper (Tables V, VI), hardware equivalent to the paper's testbed is needed:

    • GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24GB VRAM)
    • CPU: Intel Xeon Gold 6330

  • Recommended Minimum Hardware (for Llama 3 8B): To reproduce the main claims with the default Llama 3 8B model, a system with a modern NVIDIA GPU and at least 16GB of VRAM is recommended.

  • Commodity Hardware / Functional Validation Path: For evaluators using commodity desktops or laptops with less powerful GPUs (e.g., 6GB-8GB VRAM), all claims can still be fully validated. The artifact scripts are configured to automatically use the gpt2 model (which is also evaluated in the paper, e.g., Table IV, VI) if the local path for Llama 3 8B is not found. gpt2will run on most modern commodity GPUs.

Software Requirements

  • OS: A modern Linux distribution (e.g., Ubuntu 22.04).
  • Python: Version ≥3.10≥3.10.
  • NVIDIA Stack:
    • CUDA ≥11.8≥11.8 (as specified in requirements.txt).
    • NVIDIA Driver compatible with the installed CUDA version.
  • Python Packages: All dependencies are listed in requirements.txt. The main requirements are:
    • torch
    • transformers
    • scipy
    • pandas
    • openpyxl

Other Requirements

  • Internet Connection: Required for installing Python packages via pip and for downloading the Hugging Face models. The gpt2 model (approx. 500MB) will be downloaded automatically.

metadata.title: Bond: Constraint-Directed Fuzzing for Automated Validation of Taint Analysis Results in Linux-based IoT Firmware
metadata.description:
Bond

  • Artifact for USENIX Security '26 Submission

  • 《Constraint-Directed Fuzzing for Automated Validation of Taint Analysis Results in Linux-based IoT Firmware》

Overview

Bond is a directed fuzzing framework for the automated validation of taint analysis reports. Based on the (source, sink, call traces) information contained in the reports, Bond performs entry point identification, constraint analysis, and black-box validation. To use Bond, some environment configuration is required, after which the tool can be executed from the command line. The inputs are firmware binaries together with taint analysis reports, and the expected output is a proof of concept. During execution, Bond also generates intermediate output files, such as path constraint analysis results and entry point identification results.

Dependencies

  • Python 3.7

  • Java 8 (1.8.0_202)

  • npm 10.8.2

  • Python packages (see requirements.txt)

  • IDA Pro 7.5

Configuration

Since we have modified the underlying mutation logic of BooFuzz, and our constraint analysis is built on EmTaint, which requires changes to the core code of Angr, you will need to replace several library files. We have provided the necessary patched libraries and their relative paths under the third_party directory.

run_para.py: Contains device-specific configurations, such as login credentials and IP addresses.

dataflow.conf: Contains directory configurations, for example, you need to specify the path to your IDA Pro engine here.

Usage

  1. Setup the testing environment;

  2. Run Bond in the following way:

    python Bond.py -f "DIR816_1.10CNB05" -b "goahead"

  3. Check the output and the result folder for results.

Important Files and Directories

Path Description
Bond_result/firmware_complete/ Full dataset of processed firmware-(Dataset)
Bond_result/firmware_final/ Final dataset used in experiments-(Dataset)
Bond_result/static_report/ Aligned Taint Analysis Reports from Four Tools-(Dataset)
Bond_result/action_find/ Entry Point Identification Results-(Output)
Bond_result/custom_analysis/ Path Constraint Analysis Results-(Output)
fuzz_log/fuzz_sent_log.txt Proof of Concept (PoC)-(Output)

CVE Reports

This dataset is used for validating known vulnerabilities. It is located at:

Bond_result\custom_analysis\A3002R_1.1.1

Here, A3002R_1.1.1 represents the firmware model. For example, within this folder you will find:

A3002R_1.1.1_boa_CVE_reports.json

This JSON file already contains the annotated vulnerability points. You can directly feed it into Bond to perform validation.

metadata.title: SkeleShare: Algorithmic Skeletons and Equality Saturation for Hardware Resource Sharing
metadata.description:
This artifact contains logic to evaluate the effectiveness of SkeleShare, as presented in SkeleShare: Algorithmic Skeletons and Equality Saturation for Hardware Resource Sharing, an upcoming CGO'26 paper.

SkeleShare is a fully automated system for resource allocation and hardware sharing in functional FPGA compilation. It combines:

  • a multi-abstraction skeleton IR,
  • equality saturation to explore all legal transformation sequences,
  • a solver‑based extractor that jointly decides allocation and sharing under device constraints,
  • and a structured lowering pipeline that targets the SHIR compiler and Intel FPGA toolchains.

The Docker image in this artifact reproduces the paper's main results, which are found in Table III and Figure 12. VHDL code for all experiments can be generated using a single command inside the container, and results are written to the local results/ directory for inspection and further processing.

Docker Image: skeleshare-cgo26-artifact_image.zip
Pre-computed Results: precomputed.zip

metadata.title: RAVEN: Software for automated sleep microstructure analysis from electroencephalography.
metadata.description:
This software specialises in the automated detection and analysis of sleep-related microstructures, including sleep spindles, K-complexes, delta waves, and cyclic alternating patterns, directly from raw EEG signals. It identifies these microstructures without the need for prior sleep staging, utilising signal-derived parameters and multi-thresholding techniques to ensure accurate detection.

The software features an intuitive GUI that requires no prior coding experience, making it accessible to all users. Through this interface, users can easily adjust the detection thresholds to better suit their specific needs. 

The software accepts EEG files in European Data Format (EDF) or SleepLab format (SLF). It supports both batch analysis, where all files in the input folder are processed in one go, and individual analysis, allowing for the examination of selected file. Software allows user to select which specific sleep microstructures to analyse, or to select all available options for a compherensive analysis.

RAVEN is developed using MATLAB (version 2024a). Users must have MATLAB (R2023a or later) installed to run the software. To access the RAVEN, users need to download all necessary files (Main_code, RAVEN, and RAVEN_UI) into same folder and execute the Main_code through MATLAB, which will launch the GUI.

RAVEN is intended for research use only.

metadata.notes:
Version 1.5 Release Notes

Overview

Version 1.5 incorporates minor bug fixes, functional enhancements, and updated default threshold settings derived from manually scored annotations used in the validation study. This release requires MATLAB R2023a or later due to compatibility changes introduced in recent updates.

Validation

RAVEN has now been validated using three independent datasets:

  • Montreal Archive of Sleep Studies (MASS)

  • CAP Sleep Database

  • SmartSleep Lab (SSL) recordings from the University of Eastern Finland, Kuopio, Finland

A manuscript describing the complete validation workflow and results is currently under review. A minor update will be released once the manuscript is accepted to include citation details and any corresponding adjustments.

Minor Fixes

  • Corrected grammatical issues across the documentation

  • Clarified user instructions

  • Expanded and refined inline code comments

  • Updated graphical user interface (GUI) elements

  • Resolved indexing issues occurring during CAP analysis

  • Resolved data-handling issues when processing SLF-format files

  • Enhanced overall code stability to reduce runtime errors and improve reliability

Improvements

Thresholds and Parameterization

  • Default detection thresholds are now integrated directly into the GUI.

  • These thresholds were applied across all datasets included in the validation study, demonstrating that they function effectively as a consistent and robust starting point.

  • The default values are derived from manually scored annotations across the validation datasets and are tuned specifically to healthy-subject data.

  • Users are advised to review and adjust these thresholds when working with datasets that differ substantially from healthy populations, including pathological data where microstructure characteristics may be altered.

Performance and Usability

  • Integrated a more efficient EDF reader that also allows users to interrupt the reading process.

  • Enabled CAP detection using a single signal when appropriate for specific analyses.

Algorithmic Enhancements

Substantial improvements have been made to RAVEN’s detection algorithms:

  • Replaced wavelength and zero-crossing–based K-complex detection with canonical waveform comparison, improving detection accuracy.

  • Improved and redesigned event detection for both K-complexes and sleep spindles.

  • Modified the Hilbert transform–based envelope method to perform peak detection across all event types, enhancing separation between true events and artifacts.

  • Strengthened artifact-detection logic for all event categories.

  • Refined wavelength computation for delta waves.

  • Updated metadata and information saved during CAP analysis.

Publication Notice

Version 1.5 serves as the official release version for publication. A link to the accepted manuscript will be added on Zenodo when it becomes available.

Future Development

The upcoming RAVEN 2.0 release will introduce:

  • Automated arousal detection

  • A dedicated graphical interface for reviewing and editing detected events

  • Functionality to adjust event onsets/offsets and remove clear false positives

  • Support for user-defined threshold modification to accommodate pathological datasets in which conditions such as sleep apnea may alter typical microstructure thresholds

Future studies will characterise how specific pathological conditions influence sleep microstructures, and these findings will further inform and refine threshold customisation within RAVEN.

 

More details will be provided as development progresses.

hits.title: RAVEN: Software for automated sleep microstructure analysis from electroencephalography.

metadata.title: Petra: Trustworthy and Confidential SBOM Exchange
metadata.description: Petra is a research prototype for confidential SBOM exchange that combines structured SBOM trees, Merkle-style integrity verification, and CP-ABE–based access control. It enables fine-grained, policy-driven disclosure of SBOM contents while preserving confidentiality and verifiability. This artifact provides a fully reproducible evaluation environment and scripts to reproduce the performance and storage overhead results reported in the accompanying paper.
